title: Private Deployments — VPC & On‑Prem Deployment Guide, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback, and Customer Requirements Library
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference best practices and prescriptive steps for private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It covers reference architectures, packaging options, a pre‑deployment customer requirements library, day‑2 operations (monitoring, scaling, backups), and formal upgrade + rollback procedures. Target audience: platform engineers, SREs, solutions engineers, and customer infrastructure teams.

Scope and intent

- Scope: Production private deployments where Redwood Private is installed inside a customer VPC or on‑prem datacenter. Includes single‑region and multi‑AZ VPC architectures and on‑prem bare‑metal / VM packaging.
- Intent: Provide a single, audit‑ready reference that reduces deployment variance and shortens onboarding time for customers and internal delivery teams.

Quick summary of recommended topology

- Small/PoC: 1 control plane VM + 2 worker nodes (1-2 GPUs each) behind private LB; 3x replicas for database/metadata.
- Production single‑region: 3 control‑plane replicas (HA), GPU worker pool (N nodes) across 3 AZs, managed object storage for model artifacts, and dedicated logging/metrics cluster.
- Multi‑region / DR: Active/standby control plane per region, cross‑region backups, and cross‑region traffic failover policy.

Reference architectures (high level)

1) VPC — cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure)

- Components: VPC, public/private subnets, NAT gateways, internal load balancer (ILB), control‑plane cluster (k8s / managed k8s), GPU worker node pool, Redis KV cache, S3‑compatible artifact store, Postgres metadata DB (HA), and metrics/observability (Prometheus + Grafana + Loki).
- Network segmentation: Management plane (customer‑facing APIs), Inference plane (GPU workers only), Monitoring plane (metrics/logs), and Admin/Jumpbox subnet.

2) On‑prem — air‑gapped or customer DC

- Packaging: OVA/container images + Helm charts or operator for orchestration. Support runs on VMware ESXi, RHEL/CentOS VMs, or Kubernetes (RKE/AKS‑like distributions).
- Integration points: Customer KMS/HSM for key management, on‑prem object storage (MinIO) or NFS for artifacts, and Syslog/ELK for logs.

Pre‑deployment customer requirements library (checklist)

- Identity and access
  - Dedicated service account with least privilege for deployment automation.
  - SSH bastion/jump host access for initial installs.
- Network
  - CIDR allocations for control, worker, monitoring subnets. Recommended: /20 for medium deployments.
  - Required ports (example):
    - 443 (control plane API, LB)
    - 9000 (artifact store / MinIO)
    - 5432 (Postgres) — restrict to DB subnet and control plane IPs
    - 6379 (Redis) — internal only
    - 9100-9200 range (node exporters)
- Compute and storage
  - GPU instance types: NVIDIA A10/A30/A100 depending on perf needs. For inference quantized models consider A30/A10.
  - Local NVMe for KV cache (recommended 200–500 GB depending on model footprint).
  - Persistent storage for Postgres: 100–500 GB IOPS‑guaranteed (production).
- Security and compliance
  - KMS access or HSM integration details (key ARN, rotation schedule).
  - Audit logging destination and retention policy (recommended 90–365 days).
- Observability
  - Prometheus endpoint, Grafana access, and log shipping (Loki/ELK).
- Operational contacts and maintenance windows
  - Primary infra contact, SRE on‑call escalation path, and weekly maintenance window.

Pre‑deployment checklist (table)

| Area | Minimum requirement | Recommended | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Control plane vCPU | 4 vCPU per replica | 8 vCPU | Customer infra |
| Control plane memory | 16 GB | 32 GB | Customer infra |
| Worker GPU | 1 GPU (A10/A30) | Multi‑GPU pool (A30/A100) | Customer infra |
| Artifact storage | 1 TB | 5+ TB S3/MinIO | Platform |
| Backup retention | 7 days | 30 days+ | Platform |

Packaging and installation options

- Kubernetes (recommended for cloud/GKE/EKS/AKS): Helm chart + Operator. Use the provided helm values.yaml template and follow the k8s install script.
- On‑prem VMs: OVA images with systemd services — provide install.sh that performs package installation, systemd unit registration, and service start.
- Air‑gapped: Provide tarballs of OCI images and an image registry bundle + offline install instructions.

Example install flow (k8s)

1. Prepare cluster and namespace:
   - kubectl create namespace redwood-private
   - Apply node‑selector and taints to GPU nodes: kubectl label nodes gpu-01 redwood=worker && kubectl taint nodes gpu-01 redwood=worker:NoSchedule
2. Upload artifacts to S3/MinIO and set artifacts.bucket in helm values.
3. helm install redwood-private ./charts/redwood-private -f values-production.yaml
4. Verify: kubectl get pods -n redwood-private and ensure all pods reach Running in < 5 minutes for control plane, worker pods may take longer for GPU drivers.

Network and firewall requirements (detailed)

- Allowed inbound rules to control plane LB: 443 from customer CIDR(s).
- Internal ports between control plane and workers: 7000–7100 (gRPC control), 8500 (model pull), 6379 (Redis).
- Healthcheck endpoints: /healthz on control plane (HTTP 200 required).

Day‑2 operations: runbook and procedures

- Monitoring and SLOs
  - SLOs (suggested): 99.9% control‑plane API availability, 95% inference requests < 200 ms P50 for small models, P99 < 1200 ms (depends on model).
  - Alert thresholds (examples):
    - Control plane pod restart > 3 in 10m — P1
    - Inference error rate > 1% over 5m — P1
    - Redis memory > 80% — P2
- Routine maintenance tasks
  - Weekly: verify backups completed, rotate attestations, check disk pressure.
  - Monthly: apply OS and driver patches in a canary pool.
- Scaling procedures
  - Horizontal scale workers: update the autoscaler config or patch the worker node pool (cloud) to N+X nodes.
  - Vertical scaling: increase GPU instance size for a specific pool and rolling restart worker pods with node drains.

Backups and disaster recovery

- Postgres snapshot cadence: hourly WAL archiving + daily full snapshot. Retention: 30 days (configurable).
- Artifact store: replicate to cross‑region S3 or secondary MinIO cluster nightly.
- Restore validation: weekly restore to staging cluster and run smoke evals against a standard prompt set.

Upgrade and rollback procedure (formal)

Principles:
- Prefer canary first, then progressive rollout. Always take backups and record the exact image digests. Have a rollback path validated before starting.

Step‑by‑step (k8s, Helm/Operator)

1) Pre‑upgrade checks (must succeed)
  - Verify backup completion for Postgres and artifact store.
  - Verify cluster health and < 5% pod restarts in last hour.
  - Run smoke eval against staging endpoint and store results.
2) Canary upgrade
  - Deploy new image to 1 canary control plane replica and a small worker subset.
  - Observe canary for 15–60 minutes: metrics (latency, errors), logs for exceptions, and model serving correctness via canned prompts.
3) Progressive rollout
  - If canary is OK, increase rollout to 25% -> 50% -> 100% using helm upgrade with --set rollout.batchSize=<N>. Wait for each stage to stabilize (recommended 10–20 minutes depending on load).
4) Validation
  - Run automated post‑upgrade smoke tests (end‑to‑end inference, artifact pulls, KV cache warmup).
  - Check observability dashboards and compare to pre‑upgrade baseline.
5) Rollback procedure (if any gate fails)
  - helm rollback redwood-private <previous-release> (ensure release history is available).
  - If helm rollback fails or cluster is compromised, restore Postgres from the latest snapshot and redeploy previous images by digest.
  - Post rollback: run restore validation and trigger incident review.

Rollback cribs and tips

- Always capture image digests (sha256) not tags.
- Keep a documented migration plan if database schema changes are included in the release. Schema migrations should be backward compatible or run as a separate migration job with feature flags.
- If KV cache is corrupted during upgrade, flush cache and allow warmup via controlled traffic.

Testing and validation (pre and post upgrade)

- Pre‑upgrade: run the full CI inference harness against a staging cluster using the customer prompt set described in the customer requirements entry. Save metrics for comparison.
- Post‑upgrade: validate inference correctness with the same prompt set and compare tokenization/response distributions for regression. Use our regression triage playbook for any drift.

Operational runbook snippets (examples)

- Restart a stuck worker pod: kubectl -n redwood-private rollout restart daemonset/redwood-worker --selector=redwood=worker
- Promote standby region (DR): run dr/promote.sh --region <region-code> and update DNS failover policy.

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: eng-private‑deployments team (oncall: +1 escalation to Platform SRE).
- Oncall escalation: PagerDuty redwood‑platform -> Platform Lead -> Eng Manager.

Security considerations

- Secrets: use KMS‑backed secrets provider or Vault integration. Do not store plaintext keys in helm values.
- Hardening: restrict control plane access to specific CIDR ranges and enforce mutual TLS for inter‑service communication.

Appendix A — Example helm values (trimmed)

artifactStore:
  provider: "s3"
  bucket: "redwood-artifacts"
  endpoint: "https://minio.internal.local"
postgres:
  host: "redwood-postgres.internal"
  port: 5432
  database: "redwood"
  backupSchedule: "0 2 * * *"
redis:
  host: "redwood-redis.internal"
  port: 6379

Appendix B — Common troubleshooting commands

- kubectl get events -n redwood-private --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
- kubectl logs -n redwood-private <pod> -c control-plane
- kubectl exec -n redwood-private <pod> -- redis-cli INFO replication

Appendix C — Customer requirements mapping (example entries)

- Customer A: Requires FIPS‑compliant KMS, uses VMware, expects dedicated GPU pool and 365d audit log retention.
- Customer B: Cloud‑only (AWS), requires cross‑region artifact replication and 99.95% SLA for inference endpoints.

Related documents and references
